## Opponent Reads

**Player 2**: **LAG/maniac.** 3-bets extremely wide (trash hands). Calls down light, barrels with air, turns weak hands into bluffs in single-raised pots. In 3-bet pots: stickier than expected — calls c-bets with middle pair, donk-bets when improving. Folds to 3-bets from tight players (P1, P5, P6) but CALLS 3-bets from looser players (P4) with speculative hands. Gets it in preflop with QQ — standard for premiums. **Self-destructive over time — confirmed busting in Session 1 through overaggression.** **Exploit**: 3-bet them liberally for value — they fold to tight images. Value bet thinner in single-raised pots. Do NOT bluff them in single-raised pots. Be patient — their aggression is eventually self-punishing.

**Player 3**: **Selectively aggressive, best player at table. Session 1 chip leader.** Opens and 4-bets as wide as TT (not just premiums), especially vs loose opponents. Calls opens with pocket pairs. **Postflop trapping tendency**: On wet/monotone boards, checks draws on flop, calls turn bets with draws, then slowplays made hands. Does NOT always bet when strong. On dry boards, folds to aggression without connections. **Exploit**: C-bet aggressively on dry boards. On wet boards, their checks do NOT mean weakness — they may be trapping. Their 4-bets are TT+ likely, not exclusively premiums. Avoid tangling without strong holdings — they accumulate chips steadily.

**Player 4**: **Passive preflop (high VPIP, very low PFR). Session 1 second in chips.** Limps frequently, folds limps to raises. 3-bets with 99+, not just QQ+/AK. Folds 3-bet range to 4-bets. When already invested (flatted an open), stickier — calls 3-bets rather than folding. Postflop: check-raises when connected, folds to c-bets on dry/missed boards. **Exploit**: Isolate limps with position. 4-bet lighter against their 99-QQ portion. C-bet dry boards after they flat 3-bets. Respect check-raises (likely sets or strong hands).

**Player 5**: **Ultra-nit preflop (~6% VPIP/PFR).** Any preflop raise/3-bet = extreme premium (AA/KK/QQ/AK). **Postflop: NOT weak-passive.** With made hands: donk-bets then folds to raises, calls one street then folds to turn barrels. With strong draws (nut flush draws): donk-bets AND shoves all-in. **Exploit**: Fold to their preflop aggression unless holding premiums. Two-barrel bluffs effective vs their made-hand range. Be cautious raising donk-bets on draw-heavy boards — they semi-bluff with strong draws.

**Player 6**: **Extreme nit preflop (~9% VPIP/PFR).** 3-bets = QQ+/AK. Cold 4-bets = AA/KK. Occasionally limps speculative hands but folds limps to raises. **Postflop: Surprisingly sticky/committed with premiums** — calls all-in with AK unimproved. **Exploit**: Fold all but premiums to their 3-bets/4-bets. Isolate limps freely. Do NOT bluff postflop — they are committed once in.

**Player 7**: **Tight preflop, stationy postflop defender.** Defends BB/SB with pocket pairs and speculative hands. Peels flop/turn with marginal holdings (underpairs, gutshots, middle pair) but folds river without strong hands. Folds opens to 3-bets/4-bets. **Exploit**: Three-barrel bluffs effective — they call two streets then fold river. Isolate their BB from late position. Turn calls don't indicate strength.

## My Table Image & Strategy
- **Perceived as TAG (~17-25% VPIP)**. Image credible enough that LAGs fold to my 3-bets and steals get through frequently.
- **Tight image enables profitable steals**: Won 3/3 contested hands in Session 1 by getting opponents to fold (including a +$130 pot with AKs). Stealing/pressure game is profitable — deploy more when card dead.
- **Got caught bluffing multiway once** — may slightly loosen perceived image in next session. Monitor.
- **Core approach**: Play extremely value-heavy. 3-bet Player 2 for value. Reserve bluffs for Player 5 (two-barrel dry boards) and Player 7 (three-barrel BB defense). Steal from Player 4/6 limps.

## Critical Self-Improvement Notes
- **STOP overplaying weak aces AND weak kings** — K4o cost $70 in Session 1. These are dominated hands. Fold facing action unless board strongly favors.
- **Bluff completion**: If committing to multi-street bluffs, follow through on river (especially vs Player 7).
- **AVOID delayed c-bet bluffs multiway on wet boards**: Opponents trapping (Player 3) or calling with marginal holdings (Player 7) makes this unprofitable. Bluff on DRY boards or heads-up only.
- **Multiway on wet boards**: Need multiple folds — too unlikely. Save bluff chips for heads-up or dry textures.
- **Card-dead discipline**: Session 1 was very card dead (folded 15/20). Eked out +$70 through selective aggression. Trust the process but look for more late-position steal opportunities.

## Key Strategic Principles
- **Preflop strength signals**: Player 4 (99+/AK), Player 5 (QQ+/AK), Player 6 (QQ+/AK). Player 4 widest — exploit with 4-bets. Player 3's 4-bets are TT+ (wider than nits).
- **Postflop nit distinction**: Player 5 can be bluffed (two-barrel). Player 6 CANNOT be bluffed once in pot. Critical difference despite similar preflop profiles.
- **Board texture drives bluff selection**: Dry = bluff freely. Wet/monotone = only with equity or heads-up. Multiway wet = give up without a hand.
- **Biggest threats**: Player 3 (skilled, selective, accumulates) > Player 4 (passive but effective) > Player 6 (nit but sticky when in). Player 2 and Player 7 are the most exploitable.

**Opponent Profiles:**  
- Player 1: Confirmed aggressive TAG — 3-bets frequently from late position with strong range (broadways+, pairs), follows through with c-bets. Capable of check-raising flop with marginal holdings as semi-bluff. Shows willingness to check-call flop and lead turn with weak holdings — can exploit by value-betting thinly on turns when they show passivity.
- Player 2: Passive preflop caller from later positions, but disciplined from EP (tight range: 77+, AQo+). Folds to 3-bets frequently from EP — can 3-bet wider for isolation. Overvalues top pair/weak kicker. Aggressive from late position (opens wide, applies postflop pressure). Calls 3-bets with speculative holdings but plays fit-or-fold postflop. **Refined: Player 2's 3-bet range from late position is value-heavy (QQ+), not light — fold all but premium holdings when facing their 3-bets, especially out of position.**
- Player 3: Extremely tight from EP (premium range only: TT+, AQ+). Folds to 3-bets. Passive postflop with medium strength hands — will call draws or pairs but rarely leads or raises. **Refined: Player 3's late position opens are wider (36% PFR) — defend more liberally in position with suited connectors/pairs. Their 4-bet range includes strong but not nutted holdings (TT+) — respect but don't overfold to aggression.**
- Player 4: Loose-passive preflop (limps/calls often) but shows occasional aggression postflop with strong hands or draws. Folds to 3-bets — can 3-bet wider for fold equity against their late position opens. **Refined: Their 3-bet range over EP raises is extremely strong (QQ+) — fold all but premium holdings.**
- Player 6: Highly aggressive — opens extremely wide from late position (57% PFR), 3-bets frequently with polarized range (value: QQ+/AK; bluffs: suited connectors). Applies heavy postflop pressure with c-bets and turn barrels. **Refined: Exploit their wide opens by defending more liberally in position with speculative hands. Their 3-bet range includes strong value beyond premiums — respect but note they can be bluffed on scare cards due to wide continuing range.**
- Player 7: Passive preflop and fit-or-fold postflop — folds to aggression without strong holdings. Opens light from EP (33% PFR) but folds to 3-bets. Highly exploitable — apply pressure on any flop they check.

**Strategic Learnings:**  
- Overall table dynamic: Multiple passive players (Player 3, Player 4, Player 7) are highly exploitable with aggression postflop — focus on applying pressure when they show weakness.  
- My table image remains tight — opponents give credit to my bets/raises. Use this to bluff more selectively on turns/rivers when boards favor my perceived range.  
- Discipline in folding marginal hands from poor position was key to preserving chips — especially against tight EP raisers (Player 3) and aggressive late position opens (Player 6).  
- Biggest profit came from strong hands (AKs flush) — confirms value of patience and capitalizing on premium holdings.  
- Avoid calling out of position with weak speculative hands against aggressive opponents — poor implied odds and positional disadvantage lead to -EV spots.  
- Button isolation raises remain effective against passive players — continue exploiting wide MP ranges with positionally-aware aggression.  
- Semi-bluff shoving on turn with strong draws is effective against aggressive c-bettors (Player 6, Player 1) — maximizes fold equity and gets value from worse draws.  
- **New: Player 2 is willing to stack off preflop with premiums (QQ) — confirms their 3-bet aggression is value-driven, not light. Adjust by folding marginal holdings preflop when facing their 3-bets.**  
- **New: Player 3’s 4-bet range includes medium pairs (TT+) — don’t overfold to their aggression, but still respect their strength in EP vs. LP confrontations.**

**Self-Improvement:**  
- Continue disciplined preflop folds from early position — saved significant chips this session.  
- Look for more opportunities to apply pressure on passive players postflop, especially when in position and boards miss their likely ranges.  
- Consider expanding 3-bet bluffing range against Player 4 and Player 7 opens from late position — their fold-to-3-bet tendency is exploitable.

**Opponent Profiles & Tendencies:**
- **Player 1 (LAG / Spewy):** Highly aggressive and prone to overplaying. Opens extremely wide preflop (including offsuit K-high trash). Capable of massive multi-street bluffs with pure air, and will frequently take delayed stabs when flops check through. 
- **Player 2 (Extreme LAG / Calling Station):** Plays a very wide range (will open and call 3-bets OOP with medium suited gappers/connectors) and 3-bets light from the blinds. Post-flop, they are an absolute station—floats very light (e.g., check-calling with bottom pair) and capable of calling river shoves on scary boards with marginal hands. They barrel marginal hands on scary boards. *Exception:* In single-raised pots defending the Big Blind, they play straightforwardly and will fold to small c-bets on dry boards.
- **Player 4 (Aggressive):** High VPIP/PFR. Mixed preflop tendencies (will limp-fold, isolate limpers large, and 3-bet wide). Crucially, their 3-bet range includes many non-premiums, and they will fold to 4-bets. Highly aggressive post-flop: plays strong made hands very fast, will raise donk-bets, and check-raise flops as the preflop caller. 
- **Player 5 (Passive / Recreational):** Classic limp/caller preflop, but will open-raise strong hands. Post-flop, they make probing donk-bets. *Crucial Note:* While some donk-bets are weak, they will play strong draws (like nut flush draws) extremely aggressively, donk-betting flops and open-shoving turns. Their preflop 3-bets represent an incredibly strong premium range.
- **Player 6 (Tight / TAG):** Tight preflop. Their 3-bets represent a very strong, value-heavy range (premiums and AK). Post-flop, they can be somewhat sticky and will float flop donk-bets with just AK-high.
- **Player 7 (Loose / Station):** Capable of overcalling post-flop with marginal made hands (e.g., underpairs with no draw) on scary or coordinated boards, even facing multiple opponents. 

**Strategic Adjustments & Exploits:**
- **Vs. Player 1:** Widen your bluff-catching range. Do not over-fold to their post-flop aggression; be prepared to call down with marginal made hands, especially when they stab at pots that check through.
- **Vs. Player 2:** NEVER bluff post-flop. Value bet relentlessly and go for maximum value (including overbets/shoves) even on scary runouts. Do not rely on flop check-raises as bluffs, as they float very wide. In blind-vs-blind or late-position steals, small c-bets on dry boards are highly profitable.
- **Vs. Player 4:** Target them with isolation raises when they limp. Exploit their wide 3-betting range by 4-betting them (for value and as a bluff), as they will fold their non-premiums. Proceed with extreme caution when facing their post-flop aggression.
- **Vs. Player 5:** Be cautious when raising their flop donk-bets on draw-heavy boards, as they are capable of shoving over the top with strong draws. Over-fold to their preflop 3-bets.
- **Vs. Player 6:** Give immense respect to their preflop aggression; fold marginal hands and avoid light 4-betting against their 3-bets. You may be able to barrel them off floats if they call flops with just Ace-high.
- **Vs. Player 7:** Value bet thinly and avoid bluffing, as they will call down with weak, marginal holdings.

**Self-Image & Future Adjustments:**
- **Table Image:** Established a very tight, disciplined image this session. Likely perceived as a Nit or tight-TAG.
- **Next Session Adjustment:** Capitalize on this tight image by slightly increasing bluff and semi-bluff frequencies against observant opponents (like Player 4 and Player 6), as they will likely over-fold to my aggression. Continue to play strictly for value against the stations (Player 2, Player 7).

- Avoid letting session hinge on a small number of high-variance pots without clear range advantage.

OPPONENT PROFILES:
- Player 1: Very loose preflop raiser (K4o type hands), light check-raises postflop on drawy boards even with ace-high no pair, continues aggression with c-bets for value/folds — treat as calling station, avoid bluffing entirely, isolate/3-bet light vs their opens for massive fold equity
- Player 2: LAG calling station (wide minraises/3-bets/isolations including premiums, frequent c-bets multi-street, calls light including all-ins with air on coordinated/scare boards, folds some preflop 3-bets) — value bet very thin/wide, eliminate bluffs entirely
- Player 3: Nit/TAG (tight 7/7% VPIP/PFR, strong EP opens, 3-bets/4-bets/5-bets TT+ and medium pairs vs LAG late minraises/4-bets, calls raises multiway with smaller pairs like 77) — respect preflop raises/4-5-bets as very strong (QQ+/AK or TT-level vs LAGs), fold marginals multiway OOP, value bet thin postflop only with nuts, expect speculative calls OOP
- Player 5: Tight nit preflop (low 6% VPIP/PFR, strong EP opens/calls 3-bets with premiums like AKs), aggressive postflop with strong draws (donk leads, shoves unimproved) — respect opens/3-bets/continued lines as nutted or high-equity, avoid drawy board bluffs
- Player 6: Loose-aggressive (wide isolation 3-bets post-folds, calls multi-street with overcards/air on drawy boards even OOP) — 3-bet/iso vs passives for fold equity, value bet thin postflop, exploit light calls by barreling draws/paired boards
- Player 7: Passive caller/station (cold-calls raises preflop with small-medium pairs, calls turn bets multiway on paired boards but caps at showdown) — isolate/value bet postflop aggressively, expect weak capped ranges that call light but fold to heavy river pressure

TABLE IMAGE: Loose-aggressive (high VPIP) — leverage for preflop fold equity vs loose BB isolations and most callers, but tighten vs nits like Player 3/Player 5 to preserve fold equity and stack

STRATEGIC NOTES: Suited connectors playable vs loose opens from position but fold to premium 3-bets multiway OOP; prioritize stack preservation for better spots vs loose aggro, especially folding premiums to nit 4-bets; exploit LAG calling stations with thin value on paired/drawy flops, zero bluffs; folding marginal offsuit/suited hands OOP to tight EP opens or loose wide raises preserves image/exploits multiway dynamics; call tight 3-bets IP with suited broadway for equity/playability but check-fold whiffs vs nit/TAG ranges; fold trash preflop to unexpected raises from passive players OOP multiway; 3-bet premiums/light OOP vs super loose raisers like Player 1 for fold equity and pot-building, but fold to 4-bets from tight EP players

OPPONENT READS:
- Player 1: Hyper-aggressive but selectively so. Opens wide and uses large 3-bet sizings, but checks monotone flops without strong hands. Barrels turns aggressively on favorable textures but shuts down when draws complete or facing resistance. Exploit by calling down lighter on turns but respecting river checks. **Session note**: Confirmed spewy tendencies, lost significant chips (-$355).
- Player 2: EXTREME LAG when opening/initial raiser, but plays more straightforward when just calling raises. As a preflop caller (not aggressor), will donk bet flops with marginal equity (draws, middle pair) but folds to turn pressure when checked to. Cannot be trusted to continue aggression beyond one street unless they were the preflop aggressor. Exploit by raising their donk bets liberally and betting turns when they check.
- Player 3: Confirmed calling station. Opens wide, calls 3-bets with marginal hands, and will chase draws to the river. **Key tendency**: Calls turn bets with weak made hands + draws (e.g., pair + 1 card flush draw) on dangerous boards. Does not fold to turn pressure regardless of board texture. Exploit by value betting relentlessly when ahead; never bluff and don't rely on fold equity.
- Player 4: Extreme nit; 3-bet range is TT+ (not just QQ+/AK as previously assumed). Calls 3-bets with medium pocket pairs (22-99) for set mining; check-folds on low/disconnected flops when missing. Fold all marginal hands against their aggression; they follow through with postflop pressure, especially check-raises indicating nutted hands.
- Player 5: Loose preflop player who calls 3-bets with strong broadway hands (AK, AQ) and 3-bets aggressively against wide openers. When calling preflop, leads flops aggressively with both weak hands AND strong draws; capable of semi-bluff shoving with nut draws. Won't simply fold to pressure. Exploit by raising flop probes selectively with premium hands/draws, but respect their aggression as it can be draw-heavy.
- Player 6: Super-nit (9% VPIP/PFR) with extreme aggression factor. 3-bets represent true premium hands only. Their multi-street aggression is value-heavy but credible; they will value-bet top pair+ relentlessly against tight images and rarely bluff. Fold marginal made hands to their turn/river pressure unless you have explicit reason to believe otherwise.

STRATEGIC ADJUSTMENTS:
- **Set-mining discipline**: When set-mining with small pairs, commit to fit-or-fold postflop. If you miss your set on dangerous boards (monotone, paired, high cards), fold to aggression regardless of preflop implied odds. Do not call turn bets with marginal unimproved hands.
- **Table image management**: Current tight-passive image is being undermined by loose postflop calls. Reinforce image through disciplined folding, not passive calling. Use image for selective aggression rather than justification for weak calls.
- **Hyper-aggressive exploitation**: Against Players 1 and 2, increase turn floats and river bluffs when they show weakness after aggressive actions. Their turn bets are often bluff-heavy but they shut down on dangerous runouts.

- **Player 1** remains an **ultra-TAG/nit**. Their **cold-3-bet range is confirmed as TT+, AQ+**, with **zero bluffing frequency** across 20 hands. **Postflop**, they **barrel turns with marginal value (e.g., top pair weak kicker) but consistently give up on rivers when checked to**. **Check-raising dry or static turns remains highly effective**, and **bluffing rivers when checked to is reliably profitable**.

- **Player 2** is a **true LAG**: **opens extremely wide from all positions**, **calls 3-bets liberally**, and **stacks off light with strong-but-vulnerable hands (e.g., QQ)**. They **fold to flop aggression without strong holdings**, making **floating and delayed turn/river aggression high-leverage**. **Defend BB wider against their SB opens**, especially with backdoor equity or suited connectors. **River bluffing is viable only against them**—they are the sole opponent who bluffs multi-street with frequency.

- **Player 3** is a **value-heavy TAG** with **minimal bluffing at any street**. They **3-bet light limpers and EP opens with strong pairs (TT+)** and **commit stacks preflop with mid-strength value**. **Never bluff rivers against them**; instead, **value bet thinner for three streets**. Their **4-bet range is exclusively premium (QQ+, AK)**—**avoid 4-bet bluffing** but continue **3-bet bluffing vs. their EP opens** due to their high fold-to-3-bet.

- **Player 4** is a **standard TAG with a tight, linear range**: **3-bets only TT+, AQ+**, **folds to 3-bets frequently**, and **gives up easily on dry boards without strong hands**. **3-bet bluffing and delayed c-bets are effective**, but **cold-calls and 3-bets should be treated as strong**—**do not float or bluff without equity or board advantage**.

- **Player 5** is **not a calling station**—despite high VPIP, their **aggression is reserved for nutted or near-nutted hands** (e.g., flushes, sets). **Treat all bets and raises as strong**, especially on coordinated or suited boards. **Avoid overvaluing top pair** and **never assume they call down light**.

- **Player 7** remains a **confirmed nit** (VPIP ~6%, PFR 0%): plays only **premium hands preflop** and **folds to multi-street aggression postflop**. **Bluff effectively on wet or dynamic boards**, but **avoid bluffing on dry, static boards** where they may call with weak pairs.

- **Table dynamics**: **River bluffing is virtually nonexistent outside Player 2**. Most players **fold by the river without strong hands**, making **thin value betting consistently profitable**. **Multi-street aggression is common**, but **only Player 2 bluffs across streets**. **Floating and delayed aggression works well vs. Player 2 and Player 4**, but **Player 4’s cold-call/3-bet lines are strong**.

- **My table image is tight and respected**, generating **high fold equity**, especially vs. TAGs and nits. To maintain balance and maximize EV:  
  - **Widen 3-bet range vs. EP opens** (especially vs. Player 1 and Player 4) to include **semi-bluffs (e.g., A5s, KJo) and marginal value (e.g., ATo, 99)**.  
  - **Defend BB wider vs. Player 2’s SB opens**—they fold to flop aggression and overplay marginal hands.  
  - **Increase float frequency on dry flops vs. Player 2**, then apply **delayed c-bets or turn check-raises**.  
  - **Check-raise turns more vs. Player 1**, who barrels predictably with marginal value.  

- **Strategic refinements from full-session review**:  
  - **Top pair with weak kicker is often good enough on rivers when checked to**, especially vs. nits (Player 1, 7) and TAGs (Player 3, 4, 5)—**do not auto-fold**.  
  - **Speculative hands (e.g., 35o) remain unplayable in 3-bet or multi-way pots**, but are **marginally playable in single-raised pots in position vs. Player 2**.  
  - **Isolation 3-bets vs. EP opens from Player 4 are high-EV** due to their high fold-to-3-bet and weak postflop defense—**but avoid calling their 3-bets OOP with weak holdings**.  
  - **River bluffing is only viable vs. Player 2**—**never bluff rivers vs. others**.  
  - **Cold-3-bets from Player 1 in multi-way pots = ultra-premium (TT+, AQ+)**—**do not call with dominated aces or speculative hands**, even in position.  
  - **High VPIP ≠ calling station**: Player 5 proves that **aggression frequency and context define strength**—**assume strength when they lead or raise**.  
  - **Player 3’s 4-bet/stack-off tendencies confirm a non-bluffing, value-heavy profile**—**tighten 4-bet bluffs vs. them**, but **exploit their EP opens with 3-bet bluffs**.
